name: Sawyer Squeeze SP129 water filtration system
summary: A squeeze filter for appropriate fresh-water sources, with a cleanable hollow-fibre membrane. It is not a solution for chemical contamination, salt water or every microbiological hazard.
description: A water plan starts with choosing a suitable source and keeping treated water separate from untreated water. The Squeeze provides a portable filtration step without a pump, but it cannot turn every disaster water source into drinking water. Store safe water first, keep the outlet clean and follow public-health advisories. The SP129 package must be checked separately from the filter family specifications.

specs.label: Membrane
specs.value: 0.1 micron absolute hollow fibre, per Sawyer

specs.label: Bottle connection
specs.value: Standard 28 mm bottle threads; check a secure fit

specs.label: Filter mass
specs.value: Approximately 3 oz for the filter, not the full kit

specs.label: Maintenance
specs.value: Backwashing with clean water according to Sawyer instructions

specs.label: Documented kit family
specs.value: Pouches, cleaning equipment and adapters are described; exact SP129 Canadian bundle unverified

pros: No battery is needed for the squeeze filtration step.
Bottle and pouch options allow different packing arrangements.
cons: Cleaning supplies and a suitable source are still necessary.
The membrane does not remove dissolved chemicals, heavy metals or salt.
This filter must not be treated as a virus purifier or radiation treatment.
useCases: Plan fresh-water filtration on a trip only after assessing the source and local health advice.
Pair a filter with stored drinking water and a separate clean collection container.

safetyNotes: Do not rely on this filter to remove viruses, chemicals, heavy metals, salt or radioactive contamination.
Sawyer advises replacement after suspected freezing of a wetted filter or other damage; apparent flow is not an integrity test.
Prevent contact between untreated water and the clean outlet or collection container. Follow local drinking-water advisories.
